findings.title: Protocol authority and executable drift
closure_evidence: PF-001 at 0acaba7f25f228477908c2c4bc81a69609f4b682: all five artifacts the authority record classes as prototypes carry the gate, their normative owner and every recorded incompatibility and prohibited use in their own source, enforced by validate_artifact_quarantine.py.

PF-004 at f98a31502f6863e0c29dc97c0f3b233c919d1b32: every mutable aggregate declares revision_model, transaction_boundary and outbox, with the four combinations outbox_events.unique(aggregate_id, aggregate_revision) forbids rejected by validate_state_vocabularies.py.

PF-002 at 2d9935ee7cc5c950b68243a671395776f31e20b8: nothing read a CDDL rule name against a vector file in either direction, so the exact-byte vectors could have encoded a different message entirely and passed. The acceptance was unsatisfiable as written — zero of the 26 rule names appear in either file, because both hold hex. cddl_instance.py now decodes both payloads and header maps, requires each to satisfy its rule with the exact label set, and re-encodes to the committed bytes; the pinned, corpus-pinned and declared-unpinned rule sets must partition the grammar exactly. VIBEPROOF_V1_CANONICAL_PROFILE.md was a second document owning canonical encoding while describing the eleven-field shadow codec, which is this finding in one file.

PF-003 at 2d9935ee7cc5c950b68243a671395776f31e20b8: the evidence-ceiling check did not exist. run_evals.py admitted authority_class and evidence_ceiling to its allowlist with a comment saying they carry no execution semantics, and read neither; one suite of 27 carried them. All 27 now do, the vocabulary is declared once in artifact-authority-v1.json and read rather than copied, and a manifest binding no fixtures caps at none so absence lowers the ceiling instead of escaping the check. What remains for SR-005 is outside this finding: protocol/vibeproof-v1.cddl is unquarantined while four of its consumers are exploratory prototypes, and registering it needs a notice inside protocol/, which this phase may not write.

findings.title: OAuth, linked identity, recovery, and ranked identity
closure_evidence: PF-005 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: the OAuth provider registry exists and the mix-up control is evaluable. /auth/github/callback declared the RFC 9207 iss parameter and /auth/x/callback did not, while reason-codes-v1.json bound OAUTH_ISSUER_MISMATCH to both; the parameter deferred to a stored provider-capability record that did not exist, so ADR-015's control could not be evaluated at all. Sixteen mix-up vectors are derived from the registry rather than listed.

PF-006 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: every identity mutation reaches one transaction. linkIdentity took a bare authorization_code, so redirect, state, PKCE, provider revision and lifetime were optional in practice; oauth_transactions now binds all eighteen bindings the contract names, four as check constraints, and intended_action had no CHECK at all in the DDL while the API spelled it snake_case.

PF-007 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: unlinking a provider account was silently permanent product-wide: provider_subject was not null under a total unique (provider, provider_subject), so a retained unlinked row blocked that provider account from ever being linked to any account, and DATA_MAP.md's delete-on-unlink promise could only be honoured by deleting the row the constraint required. Both personal-data fields are now null exactly when the binding has ended.

PF-008 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: consolidation has a path. The account-consolidation machine declares consolidation-confirm with actor user and the API declared no consolidation operation at all, so a case left awaiting-confirmation only by expiring. D-564, that the older ranked identity survives, was recorded in no machine-readable place and is now checkable with a matched negative fixture.

findings.title: Device lineage, challenge, replay, checkpoint, and recovery
closure_evidence: PF-009 at 48b22762fcce6d84650f352867f717ae9df41920: device_sequences keys on lineage_id and no longer references a device row, continuity_state has one owner in device_lineages, and claim_challenges carries a lineage_id foreign key. A copied device store previously produced two internally continuous rows, making the fork invisible to the counter meant to catch it.

PF-010 at c7647fe7bb1f171588106de8c14d9f20cdb4be34: lineage scoping was enforced where the sequence counter is read and not where it is written. D-592 rekeyed device_sequences onto the lineage and stopped one table short: claims still carried unique (device_id, device_sequence) and unique (device_id, payload_hash), so two device rows in one lineage could each hold sequence 42 and the same payload. checkpoint_receipts was device-keyed while the head it advances was lineage-keyed, giving a restored store a private receipt chain. device_key_events could not record dual authorization at all — one nullable signature and no account column — so an ordinary rotation and a single-signature forgery were the same row. All three are repaired, with recovered forbidding the outgoing signature so a rotation cannot be admitted by claiming to be a recovery. AUTHENTICATION_AND_RECOVERY.md also ended the recovery order with a human appeal, contradicting D-561's accepted rule that exhaustion is permanent.

PF-070 at 32638ddb6235e2105ca1f38dcef11a803e6e60b7: the fourth conflicting artifact is repaired. openapi-v1.yaml#ClaimChallenge was named by this finding and touched by no unit; the challenge was defined three times over disjoint fields, so the expected sequence, local head and checkpoint tuple the protocol says the server verifies was persisted nowhere and the API carried a batch_commitment neither other authority had. Eleven fields now agree across the CDDL, the DDL and the API, with a validator failing on a field present in one and absent from another in either direction, and four server-only columns each recording why. batch_commitment was removed rather than propagated because every claim signs the challenge nonce, so a digest over the batch cannot be computed before the challenge that binds it exists — it was uncomputable in all three places. What remains is outside this finding: checkpoint-receipt-v1 and checkpoint_receipts have near-disjoint columns and server_receipt_sequence is stored nowhere, which keeps D-043 provisional.

findings.title: Local daemon, shell, IPC, and platform supervision
closure_evidence: PF-011 at 355755b365f3b1ee0ac158255af21a103303ea1d: all eight local roles are declared once in packages/schemas/local-trust-domains-v1.json with an OS peer identity per platform, a session boundary, an explicit network scope and capability, data-class and prohibition lists. PLATFORM_KEY_AND_PRIVILEGE_MATRIX.md tabulated six and omitted the interactive shell and the privileged supervisor — the only role taking arbitrary operator input and the only one running elevated. The separation the privacy boundary rests on is enforced: exactly one role may read transcript-content and its network scope is none. The local channel protocol, shell/subsystem separation and local persistence remain open under PF-012, PF-013 and PF-014.

PF-012 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: local-control-v1.proto reaches every message body only through its own role's arm, so a collector encoding a deletion request is unrepresentable rather than rejected. Envelope previously carried one universal oneof holding all fifteen bodies with sender_role a field the sender filled in, while LOCAL_IPC_AND_DEVICE_IDENTITY.md stated that role confusion is rejected. Three local-channel reason codes now exist for what remains detectable; the protocol previously had no vocabulary with which to refuse anything. Shell/subsystem separation and local persistence remain open under PF-013 and PF-014.

PF-013 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: interactive-shell declares only the eight process and connection states. It previously carried fifteen, collapsing collection, sync, auth, permission, update and connectivity into one state variable, so a device with paused collection and an offline network had no representable shell state. Five projections now persist in local-store-v1.sql. Local persistence and migration remain open under PF-014.

PF-014 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: the canary fixture now covers log, backup, diagnostic and corruption-report, the four surfaces that carry content by accident rather than by design and the four the acceptance named. Repairing it found four pre-existing negative cases naming a forbidden class in snake_case where the allowlist declares kebab-case, so they resolved to nothing; a fifth naming otel-identity-attributes, which was declared nowhere; and two cases sharing one canary token, which defeats attribution. All four units serving SR-008 have landed.

findings.title: Universal adapter certification and deterministic accounting
closure_evidence: PF-015 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: the compatibility tuple's canonical digest is proved rather than asserted. The schema stated that the digest is over the RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR encoding so two implementations cannot disagree about a tuple's identity, and nothing tested it; the unit's own note recorded the digest half as not landed. Two serialisations in opposite key order at every level now produce one digest, and each of the five independent dimensions changes it. Certification lifecycle and accounting reconciliation remain open under PF-016 and PF-018.

PF-018 at bc5880ae0b3d775ee9ab45d0d46ff401ac6640be: reconciliation and bounds are specified and exhaustively ordered. The acceptance allowed the author to choose two array orderings, which a first-wins reconciler satisfies on any agreeing pair; every permutation is exhausted now under a declared cap that fails rather than sampling. accounting-profile.schema.json spelled the fourth count authority reconstructed while nine artifacts spelled it exact-reconstruction, so a validator comparing them would have reported a contradiction that does not exist for every reconstruction profile, and did not fire only because the one binding it runs over is provider-reported. Summation across readings and selection-based contradiction resolution are forbidden, bounds reject rather than saturate, and capping is recorded forbidden because Token Burn is unnormalized. Nothing is certified: no vector names a certified tuple.

PF-071 at ea4ceafab557936b21642d362d76f251ef28b8d5: adapter-manifest.schema.json#certification, the artifact neither PF-015 nor PF-018 opened and which no commit had touched since the P-1140B freeze. It was green because nothing read it. The block now declares a required state whose enum is uncertified plus the eight states of the source-certification machine; bundle_sha256 admits null and is null exactly when the state is uncertified, bound in both directions so a forgotten digest and a declared absence of certification cannot be stated apart; modes and certification.mode both admit exactly the nine observation modes observer-equivalence-v1.json declares, so import is refused and acp admitted; and the committed example carries no invented bundle digest. Nothing is certified: every state this repository can reach is candidate or uncertified.

findings.title: Social relationships, boards, presence, and notifications
closure_evidence: PF-024 at f7db7bb052cf8fef10f72ff8cbae802d13d1cf51 (social relationships only): blocked is removed from the friendship and rivalry machines and from friend_requests.state and rival_edges.state, so a directional block no longer drives a symmetric aggregate to a terminal state. PF-027 at e253dfa65b4802bf6fba87ce404ec575cf5232ba: notification categories, the inbox and the channel model are bound. findings.title: Idempotency and ambiguous commit recovery
closure_evidence: PF-019 at bf1a128ace7a3d6e8cccc2585270382da242aaee: idempotency_records keys on exactly the key_scope openapi-v1.yaml#x-idempotency-contract declares, so operation_id is inside the key and one key across two operations can no longer be answered with the other operation's recorded response. replayable-failure and abandoned replace a single failed state, which is the distinction a retry needs.

PF-020 at 868e4f867c65442faf51deb79f3a93738258de66: expiry was implemented as deletion, and a deleted key is a fresh key. idempotency_records had one lifetime column, so the only way to stop replaying past the window the wire contract declares was to delete the row — after which the next request carrying that key executed as a new mutation, which is the exact case the unit's prose said must be refused. retain_until now bounds retention separately from replay. sql-race-plans-v1.json asserted nothing: all fourteen cases carried the same four interleaving steps and one sentence, and the validator checked only ids, table existence and a flag, all of which pass on placeholders. Nineteen cases now name the rows a correct implementation leaves behind, present and absent, with 92 column assertions resolving against the DDL. Three stale justifications claiming this finding stays open for defects PF-019 and PF-049 had already repaired were struck.

findings.title: Export, deletion, retention, and backup tombstones
closure_evidence: PF-028 at 9f5b7e2baf82a5fa085873f294b33ccb065274ba: export authority is bound to a domain vocabulary that did not exist. The acceptance asked for included and excluded domains in a repository where no domain vocabulary existed anywhere, so any implementation satisfying it would have invented a fourth spelling, and it named the wrong table for the revocable grant, which was a stub with neither a grant nor an expiry. Seven data domains are declared once in DATA_MAP.md, carried on all 71 personal rows of the disposition registry and compared three ways; the third comparison found presence_events filed under account and identity while presence_leases sat under social.

PF-029 at 9f5b7e2baf82a5fa085873f294b33ccb065274ba: deletion_effects.state admitted not-applicable, a member meaning we did not look, so a plan could cover all seven domains by declining to answer for any; consolidation-plan-v1.schema.json refuses that value in that position, so the repair had reached one sibling and not the other. The Article 30 record promised a cancellation nothing could perform: DATA_MAP states the cooling-off window as cancellable and the machine had no cancelled state and no route to one. And the acceptance's own grep for an erasure overclaim passed on a document that had never contained the word, which is an absence satisfied by emptiness inside the criterion written to prevent one.

findings.title: Release authorization, compatibility, migration, and rollback
closure_evidence: PF-030 at ecb67d7d15d917956c48309f8201c52918c52211: the release-set schema requires the eight per-component fields and, more importantly, refuses the case its acceptance could not state: a manifest is itself a target, so a release set whose manifest is signed by the root role or whose manifest target path is a component path authenticates itself. Seven negative examples name one refusal each and each must be exercised.

PF-031 at ecb67d7d15d917956c48309f8201c52918c52211: an ordered chain and an ordered set are not the same claim, and the acceptance asked only for order — a migration list can be sorted, complete-looking and still skip a version, after which a rollback walks off the end of it. Contiguity is checked and a gap is a named negative example. install-plan-v1.schema.json gained the plan_kind discriminator this exposed: platform_install_plans was keyed on profile and release alone, so install, upgrade, repair, uninstall and orphan cleanup were the same row.

PF-032 at ecb67d7d15d917956c48309f8201c52918c52211: installability and competitive eligibility are separated in a way that buys something. Two booleans satisfy the word separately; what is enforced now is that the combination which occurs — installable and not competitively eligible, which is what a container and a CI runner are — is representable, and that a profile asserting eligibility with no supervision mechanism to derive it from fails.

findings.title: Current-authorization recheck at every display and delivery boundary
closure_evidence: PF-021 at 7891df41e9fb4b27c7fae378beea67a9aed7e971 (getPublicProfile only): getPublicProfile required no viewer while projection-authorization-v1.json made directional-block deny-hard, so a blocked person could read the profile by logging out. It now requires a session and returns 401 without one. The recheck at every other display and delivery boundary is not done.

PF-021 at 986e90c29eba7733456e48cd95f99d88c3a32d0f: PF-021 completed here and the completion was recorded against SR-010 only, while the unit serves both. getLeaderboard is a conflicting artifact of this finding as well as of SR-010, and it held the global-board public reason while its path admitted global, friends, rivals and board — so GET /leaderboards/friends/weekly answered an unauthenticated caller with a viewer-relative standing, which is this finding's invariant failing at a boundary this finding names. The entry is added because the evidence existed and was filed in one of the two places it belonged, not because anything new landed.

PF-022 at 986e90c29eba7733456e48cd95f99d88c3a32d0f: the snapshot boundary is the one this finding names that no unit serving it had ever claimed. ranking-cursor-v1.schema.json now binds the viewer, the generation, the snapshot, the authorization revision and the expiry, and a presentation whose current revision differs is refused authorization-revision-moved. That is the mechanism SR-015 is about at planning-schema.sql#score_snapshots: a durable client-held handle into a sealed generation was the way a viewer kept receiving entries for a participant who had since blocked them, because the cursor contract carried no authorization state to recheck. PF-022 was recorded as serving SR-010 alone and it repaired this finding's snapshot limb; the attribution is corrected rather than the work re-done. The score_snapshots table is itself deliberately unedited and must stay so: this finding's whole assertion is that immutable history and current authorization are two records, so repairing the snapshot to carry authorization state would be the defect rather than the fix. What was repaired is the handle into it. Note that validate_finding_artifact_coverage.py reports this artifact as covered because 986e90c changed planning-schema.sql, which it did for periods, ranking_corrections and the generation keys; file-level coverage cannot see that the score_snapshots table body is untouched, and that limitation is declared in the validator's claim_scope rather than worked around here.

PF-033 at 7c76085bd325db07985fc73e89a46ac5f5d48951: current viewer authorization is joined to the fields it gates, and the join found that a blocked participant reads the global board by logging out. One leaderboard-page surface declared nine read-time inputs on behalf of three operations, one of which carries security: [] by decision, and four of the nine are viewer-subject-pair inputs whose deny-hard directional-block resolves to admit when there is no viewer. The API also declared no cache directive on any response, so a proxy could store a profile and serve it to a second viewer, making current authorization a property of whoever asked first. board-member-list was a rule about a surface no operation renders while listBlocks, which returns a third party's account on every row, had no surface at all. No third projection file was created: the two that exist already own audience and gate, and what was missing was the join.

restatement.previous_form: Privacy-safe projection and current authorization, stated as a repairable cluster with no artifact set of its own.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found no independent artifact set: the aggregates named in the original wording are already owned by SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013, so the finding could not be closed by repairing anything it exclusively owned. It is restated as the invariant it actually asserts - every display and delivery boundary rechecks current authorization instead of replaying a historical snapshot - and bound to the boundary operations where that recheck is absent today. The artifact set intentionally intersects SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013 at different sites: those findings own their aggregates, this one owns the boundary. Closure is one enumerated boundary matrix plus a current-authorization check at every listed boundary, and is not satisfied by repairing any single aggregate.

findings.title: Review-record integrity: reviewed head, evidence class, and named owners
closure_evidence: PF-034 at 9d54b2b1bc515db1ab1ced998256ecafade9e304: the schema and interface inventory was neither computed nor hand-checked: nothing resolved one of its citations in either direction, and a probe file dropped into packages/schemas/ and another into conformance/p1140e/ passed every validator in make validate. Sixty-three shipped files were owned by nothing, including local-trust-domains-v1.json, which declares the eight roles the privacy boundary rests on, and pricing-interpretation.schema.json, which had no row of any kind. Coverage is computed in both directions now, and two self-satisfaction traps found while building it are tests: a citation naming a tree root covered that whole tree, so the sentence stating the rule satisfied it, and a directory citation covered its contents, so the sentence recording that a directory has no manifest covered every file it described as uncovered.

PF-035 at 9d54b2b1bc515db1ab1ced998256ecafade9e304: the P-1140E validator's six injections are bound to the validators that own each leg. Four of the six are owned elsewhere — reachability and three-way vocabulary agreement by validate_state_vocabularies.py, generation keys, revision sources and recomputed digests by validate_planning_artifacts.py — and forcing them into one validator would put a second owner on each of those vocabularies. The block's claimed coverage was also wrong: the matrix's five owners per decision had no injection at all, so the check resolving them had never been shown to fire. SR-016 is not closed by this: PF-036 remains open because pinning the review target and reaching zero open P1 are owner acts, and this finding is the one about review-record integrity.

PF-036 at fe74bc0305d56c10752f6e723840a34cb49bd0f7: the exact-head review. review-target-v1.json pins 46bf2fa47963261d48fa80a6980de85d80cfaad8 with planning-checks run 31606983374 on that commit, the verdict PASS-WITH-EXCEPTIONS recorded by the CTO under delegated owner authority, both registry digests, and three limitations carried verbatim here and in REPAIR_HEAD_REVIEW.md - the first of which states that this review is not independent, which is the limb of this finding that cannot be closed by performing it. REPAIR_HEAD_REVIEW.md is rewritten to pin the reviewed head and to name the superseded one, e1320a6730a62a7345ad44d149a9344d3d17c1c9, rather than dropping the digest this finding cites it at. D-300 is applied and every severity the registry can carry now has a recorded ceiling, so a regrade cannot improve the counted number by moving findings out of the only severity anything counted; the exact-head check no longer reads open P1 alone, which would have let a review pass with nine open P0 findings. The named-owner limb was closed under D-195 and the suite-name limb by the shadow-codec-parity ceiling, both recorded as needing no change here rather than retro-attributed.

restatement.previous_form: Review, conformance, and launch-evidence integrity, owned by the document that states the finding.
restatement.rationale: The finding was self-owned: its normative owners were the semantic-review document that states it and the schema inventory, so its closure evidence would have been the same prose that defines it and no external record could contradict it. Ownership moves to the two machine records that own reviewed-head and evidence-class facts, and the prose review documents become conflicting artifacts. The disagreement is now machine-checkable: REPAIR_HEAD_REVIEW.md pins e1320a6, the semantic review states base 41ecb77, and review-target-v1.json is not-pinned with a null commit; separately the state-machine registry names persistence owners for 19 of its 26 machines that packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql does not define. Closure is a pinned review-target-v1.json whose commit exists and whose verdict is recorded, prose head claims equal to it, suite names that match what each suite executes, and one resolved persistence owner for every registered machine.

unmodified_artifacts.evals/suites/suites.yaml#ranking-account: The suite-name limb was resolved where it lived rather than by a unit serving this finding. `evals/suites/suites.yaml` now carries `shadow-codec-parity` with an explicit exploratory ceiling instead of a suite named for a conformance it does not execute, which is the defect this artifact was named for. Attributing that repair here would mean adding `Serves: SR-016` to a unit that did not serve it, which is the invented attribution this program exists to remove.
unmodified_artifacts.packages/schemas/state-machine-registry-: Repaired under D-195 by adjacent work, not by a unit serving this finding. Every persistence owner named in the registry now resolves to a table in `packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql`, and a validator fails when one does not, which closes the nineteen-of-twenty-six gap this artifact was cited for. As above, the commits that did it serve other findings and are not retro-attributed here.

findings.title: Source-bound evidence and verifier appraisal authority
closure_evidence: PF-017 at bc5880ae0b3d775ee9ab45d0d46ff401ac6640be (source-observation half only): source observation and normalized event now carry required operation, observer and reading identity, and the outcome vocabularies cross-resolve. They did not: observation declared aborted-unknown and unknown, the event declared aborted-known and quarantined-unknown, and no mapping existed, so an adapter observing an aborted run with an unknown remainder had to write aborted-known — recording an unknown as known. acp was missing from the observation schema's execution_mode while five other artifacts carried it, making an ACP observation unrepresentable in the schema every ACP adapter writes. TOKEN_ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md was a second vocabulary of eighteen field names existing in no schema. The OTel derivation table now states that the counter names no execution rather than implying it does.

PF-072 at 6864cf8d90216b625d3a8a29839a19ac0b7de659: the verifier appraisal half. One aggregate was described three ways and compared on ten integers: appraisal_wire_ranges() matched an integer-range pattern and so parsed ten labels of twenty-three, leaving labels 3, 5, 14 and 18 through 22 invisible to every check built on it. verifier-appraisal-v1 gained the evidence-bundle digest, both halves of the supersession chain, the certification state and the three evaluated bundle identifiers, and labels 5 and 18 admit nil because no verifier implementation is built and every capture this repository can take is bound to no certification. verifier_appraisals went from nine columns to thirty-one and holds the claim digest, the evidence digest, the seven dimensions, the validity interval and the supersession chain, with a unique index making one appraisal current per claim. evidence_profile_id is nullable, which is what CDDL label 14 and awarded_profile_id had always said and what not null made unrepresentable. appraisal-policy-v1.json now carries wire_binding and column_bindings, and validate_evidence_chain compares all three field sets in both directions, per-field nullability, and ordinal density. Three slack integer ranges fell out of tightening the range rule from greater-than to equality. verifier_appraisals is declared the aggregate's sole persistence owner against evidence_assessments, which held the same three assessed states with nothing saying which won.

unmodified_artifacts.packages/schemas/evidence-profile-policy: This file is the sole dimension authority and the repair binds the other artifacts to it rather than editing it. appraisal-policy-v1.json pins it by content digest under D-268 and copies no enum, and validate_evidence_chain fails when that digest goes stale or when appraisal-result-v1.schema.json's dimension enums diverge from these seven vocabularies in either direction. Editing it would fork the authority the repair exists to consolidate, which is why no unit touches it and none should.
unmodified_artifacts.packages/schemas/evidence-bundle-v1.cddl: Authored under D-266 as the at-rest device-local record, it already binds the claim bytes, the source receipt, the accounting profile and the arithmetic by identity and digest. The appraisal disagreement it was named beside was resolved in appraisal-result-v1.schema.json, which carries the evidence_bundle_sha256 that points at this bundle; the bundle is the referent, not a party to the disagreement. The residual risk here is coverage rather than content, and it is recorded: SCHEMA_AND_INTERFACE_INVENTORY.md states that no instance-level CDDL conformance checking exists in this repository, so nothing executes this file.
unmodified_artifacts.packages/schemas/appraisal-result-v1.sch: This file is the target the other two authorities converge on rather than the artifact holding the defect. D-267 makes it the one appraisal record replacing the three partial descriptions this finding cites, and PF-072 moved the CDDL and the DDL onto it rather than moving it. The reason recorded here previously was that a diff would mean the target had moved; that was not true when it was written, because c7647fe had already edited this file under PF-010 and PF-016, and a reason phrased as an absence is satisfied by nobody looking. It is restated as what it is: a claim about direction, not about the file being untouched. What makes it checkable is that validate_evidence_chain now compares all three field sets in both directions, so this file moving away from the other two fails here rather than being noticed by whoever reads the diff.

restatement.previous_form: Stated as a contradiction whose closure required four unwritten schemas, with an artifact set that named nothing existing.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found that authoring an absent schema is a design task rather than a disagreement between two authorities, so the finding as written could not be falsified. It is split into the two things it actually contains. The contradiction part is live and now cited: one appraisal aggregate is described three ways - vibeproof-claim-v1.cddl verifier-appraisal-v1 carries seven classification dimensions, evidence-profile-policy-v1.json enumerates the same seven dimensions as server-verifier authority, and planning-schema.sql verifier_appraisals persists only provenance, continuity and integrity state with no claim digest, evidence digest, validity interval or supersession. The design part is the four artifacts already recorded planned-missing in SCHEMA_AND_INTERFACE_INVENTORY.md; they move to planned_artifacts, because a path that does not exist cannot be cited as a conflicting artifact. Closure requires both halves: the three existing authorities agree on one appraisal record, and the four planned artifacts exist and bind the exact claim, evidence, policy and result under D-077.
